subject: Recap: Alignment & Ownerships — Next Steps for Aperture Financial Evaluation
messages:
From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@aperturefin.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@aperturefin.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:15:00 -0400
Subject: Intro: Redwood evaluation — quick recap + follow-ups

Sean — thanks again for the conversation this morning. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can get an internal calendar moving.

Top pain points we described:
- Inference latency variability causing inconsistent user experience on batch scoring (spikes during end-of-day runs).
- High per-token cost on existing managed endpoints leading to budget overruns on peak days.
- Lack of clear rollout/testing path for new model versions across our staging/production environments.

Goals for the pilot:
1) Demonstrate a steady sub-150ms median token latency for our chat flows at 10 rps.
2) Reduce per-token inference cost by at least 30% vs our current provider for embeddings-heavy workloads.
3) Establish a safe canary/rollback policy and metrics to measure quality regressions.

Decision stakeholders we noted on the call:
- Aisha Khan (AI Platform lead / product) — evaluation owner
- Liam O'Neill (Engineering manager) — POC sign-off on performance
- Procurement (procurement@aperturefin.com) — contract/terms

Procurement timeline: we target a vendor short-list by May 20 and procurement approval by June 10. Budget is earmarked in Q2 but final authority sits with finance and procurement.

Next asks from our side:
- Can you send a compact mutual action plan with milestones and owners?
- Any SOW/template we should review for procurement?
- Proposed dates for a 2-week POC and an initial runbook for measuring latency/cost.

Happy to loop anyone else; copying Liam.

Thanks,
Aisha Khan
Lead, AI Platform
Aperture Financial

From: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@aperturefin.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@aperturefin.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 11:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Intro: Redwood evaluation — quick recap + follow-ups

Aisha — great to speak with you and Liam this morning. Appreciate the clear priorities; below is a compact mutual action plan and ownership matrix we can iterate on. I attached a working XLSX (Aperture_Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.xlsx) and a short SOW template (SOW-template.pdf) for procurement to review.

--- Mutual Action Plan (draft) ---
1) Align success criteria (owner: Aisha Khan) — by 2027-05-07
   - Confirm target latency percentiles (median and p95) and cost-per-1k-tokens target.
2) POC scheduling & baseline measurement (owner: Liam O'Neill + Redwood POC lead: Marissa Cole) — start week of 2027-05-17, 2 weeks
   - Redwood will provision private POC endpoints with reserved capacity for the test window.
   - Baseline: run current traffic sample and compare latency & cost per token.
3) Performance tuning & quantization trial (owner: Marissa Cole) — 2027-05-24 to 2027-05-28
   - Try a 4-bit quantization profile and workload-aware batching; report quality deltas on core prompts.
4) Security & compliance checks (owner: Dylan Brooks) — documentation in by 2027-05-14
   - Provide SOC2 summary, data retention options, and KMS integration notes.
5) Procurement & contract review (owner: procurement@aperturefin.com + Sean Gallagher) — target sign-off by 2027-06-10

Decision criteria (short list):
- Performance: median latency meeting stated target on the POC traffic sample.
- Cost: unit economics show >=30% savings or clear path with batching/quantization to reach it.
- Reliability & rollback: canary and auto-fallback policies validated during POC.

Attachments included: Aperture_Mutual_Action_Plan_v1.xlsx, SOW-template.pdf (see attached stubs).

Quick logistics: please confirm that the POC window week (May 17) works for your infra team and whether procurement prefers an NDA first (we can provide a standard Redwood NDA via DocuSign).

If that looks right, I'll turn this into a shared Drive sheet and add owners with task-level dates.

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
(555) 555-0142

Hi Aisha / Liam / procurement — looping in Dylan and Sean as well. Quick updates from our side and concrete next steps so procurement has what it needs: 

1) POC provisioning:
- I will own provisioning and will confirm endpoint hostnames by 2027-05-16 EOD. We will provide reserved capacity for the 2-week window and a short guide with curl examples + an open-source test harness we use for latency sampling.

2) Runbook & metrics:
- Deliverable: Redwood_POC_Runbook_v1.pdf (I'll upload to the Drive link Sean mentioned). It includes sample scripts, payload sizes, and an automated comparator for median/p95 and cost-per-1k-tokens. Expect this by 2027-05-07.

3) SOW & procurement:
- Attached is a standard SOW template (SOW-template.pdf). For redlines, please send procurement's marked-up version; we aim to return a redlined copy within 3 business days.

4) Risk & security notes (owner: Dylan Brooks) — Dylan, I flagged the doc request for SOC2 summary and KMS notes; can you upload the brief by May 14?

5) Next meeting: Proposed checkpoint after week 1 of the POC — 2027-05-24 at 11:00 AM ET. Does that work for Aperture team?

DocuSign / NDA: We can provide a standard Redwood NDA. If procurement prefers DocuSign, I will send the link once procurement confirms the contact.

Action items assigned:
- Aisha: confirm decision criteria latency percentiles by 2027-05-07 (owner)

I'll create the calendar invites and upload the MAP spreadsheet to the Drive link below once Sean gives the OK.

Thanks — looking forward to a smooth POC.
